wines.name: Camille & Mathieu Apffel Avant la Tempête 2024
wines.sub: Vin de Savoie · Savoie, French Alps
facts: Clay-limestone with glacial schist and quartz
wines.flag: Low-intervention wine: check its condition. No added sulfur and no filtration, so a slight haze or a hint of reduction is normal for the style. Vinegar, cider or mousy notes would be faults. The name means "before the storm". Camille and Mathieu farm about 5 ha themselves, with no employees.
factors: Climate
Cool, Alpine. The vines sit at the foot of Mont Granier, south of Chambéry. Mountain air and cold nights keep alcohol low and acidity very high.
Soil
Clay-limestone scattered with schist and quartz left by retreating glaciers. Free-draining, poor soils give a lean, stony wine.
Grape
Jacquère: Savoie's main white grape. Neutral, light and high in acid, with citrus, green apple, white flowers and a mineral, almost salty finish.
Winemaking
Native-yeast fermentation, nothing added, bottled unfiltered without sulfur. A hands-off approach that keeps the wine taut and pure.
Producers
Mathieu grew up in the Jura and moved to Savoie in 2013; he bought vines and a cellar in 2017. Camille joined in 2020. Organic and biodynamic farming.

sat.app: Pale lemon (may show a slight haze: unfiltered)

wines.concl: Good to very good. Light and racy, with clean citrus fruit balanced by mineral length; simple but very precise.
wines.ready: Drink now. Not intended for long ageing.
exam: Savoie: Alpine, cool continental; Jacquère is the main white, with crus like Apremont and Abymes.
Compare with Ferrando's Erbaluce (Nov 3): two Alpine-foothill whites on glacial soils, both high acid and light body.
SAT condition: clean vs faulty. Practise telling natural-wine character (haze, reduction that blows off) from real faults (volatile acidity, mousiness).
wines.say: Mountain white from the French Alps: light, crisp, lemony and stony. Made with nothing added. Great with cheese.

wines.name: Guillaume Lafon Bourgogne Blanc 2024
wines.sub: Bourgogne AOC · Côte de Beaune, Burgundy, France
facts: Guillaume Lafon, son of Dominique Lafon
wines.flag: Lafon as in Comtes Lafon. Dominique Lafon, of the famous Meursault estate Domaine des Comtes Lafon, started this separate project in 2008. His son Guillaume joined in 2023, and 2024 is the first vintage under Guillaume's own name. Les Femelottes is the same Puligny site as Alvina Pernot's other Bourgogne.
factors: Site
Two parcels in Meursault and Puligny-Montrachet, just outside the village appellations. Village-level terroir sold as Bourgogne.
Vintage
2024 whites had a wet spring with mildew and poor flowering, then sun from July. Yields fell about 25–40%. The wines are cooler, finer and lower in alcohol, with clear acidity.
Grape
Chardonnay: neutral and site-expressive. Meursault leans rich and nutty; Puligny leans taut and floral.
Winemaking
Whole-cluster pressed (gentle, fewer bitter phenolics), native yeasts, about 12 months in barrel with no new oak, then a short rest in tank. Little or no lees stirring.
Producer
Made at Château de Bligny-lès-Beaune. Horse ploughing and electric tractors in the vineyards.
wines.concl: Very good. Crisp 2024 acidity balanced by ripe fruit and gentle barrel texture; more depth and length than most regional whites.
wines.ready: Can drink now, but has potential for ageing (3–5 years).
exam: White Burgundy toolkit: whole-cluster pressing, barrel fermentation, MLF, lees ageing. Here: no new oak, little stirring.
Meursault vs Puligny style: richer and nuttier vs tighter and more floral.
The library now has three 2024 Côte de Beaune whites and reds: Pernot, Guérin and Lafon.
wines.say: Meursault and Puligny fruit from the Lafon family, the son's first vintage, at a Bourgogne price.

wines.name: Bedrock Ode to Lulu Rosé 2025
wines.flag: Taste it next to last week's Gros 'Noré. The wine is an homage to Lulu Peyraud of Domaine Tempier, Bandol's most famous estate: California Mourvèdre made in the Bandol spirit. The 2025 blend is from the producer; one critic lists less Carignan.
factors: Climate
Warm Mediterranean. Contra Costa County sits inland from San Francisco Bay, hot by day with Delta breezes in the evening. Mourvèdre needs that heat to ripen.
Soil
Deep sand in Contra Costa (Oakley). Phylloxera can't survive in sand, so the vines are own-rooted and over a century old: low yields and concentrated fruit.
Grapes
Mourvèdre gives structure, savoury herbs and red fruit. Carignan adds acidity and bright fruit; a touch of Grenache adds body.
Winemaking
Picked early for low alcohol, whole-cluster pressed (direct to juice, pale colour), native yeasts, fermented and aged only in stainless steel.
Producer
Bedrock is known for rescuing California's heritage vineyards, many planted before Prohibition.
wines.concl: Very good. Ripe fruit balanced by succulent acidity; herbal and stony notes and a long finish lift it above simple rosé.
wines.ready: Drink now. Can hold a year or two.
exam: US labelling: a "California" appellation needs 100% California fruit; an AVA needs 85% from that AVA. Multi-county blends use "California".
Sandy soils resist phylloxera, which is why old own-rooted vines survive in Contra Costa (and in Colares, Portugal).
Three Mourvèdre-family links in the library: Gros 'Noré Bandol (Nov 9), this homage, and Bandol's 50% Mourvèdre rule for reds.
wines.say: California's love letter to Bandol: century-old Mourvèdre made into a pale, crisp rosé. The best $11 pour on the list.

wines.name: Arianna Occhipinti Frappato 2025
wines.sub: Terre Siciliane IGT · Vittoria, Sicily, Italy
wines.flag: Check the label for the cuvée. Occhipinti's flagship Il Frappato normally ages 12–16 months in large casks, so a 2025 on the shelf this early would be unusual. If the label says SP68, it's her younger, unoaked Frappato–Nero d'Avola blend, and the notes below will be fresher and simpler.
factors: Climate
Hot Mediterranean, but the Vittoria plateau at 250–280 m gets sea breezes and cool nights. Frappato keeps its acidity and perfume.
Soil
Sand and white limestone on an ancient seabed. Sand gives a light, perfumed style; limestone adds freshness.
Grape
Frappato: thin-skinned and pale, high in acidity, low in tannin, very aromatic (strawberry, pomegranate, rose, white pepper). Sicily's answer to Pinot Noir or Gamay.
Winemaking

Il Frappato: up to 20% whole bunches, spontaneous fermentation in concrete, 2–4 weeks on skins with gentle extraction, then 12–16 months in large 5,000 L Slavonian and Austrian casks. Unfined, unfiltered, minimal sulfur.
Producer
Arianna started in 2004 at 21, encouraged by her uncle Giusto Occhipinti of COS. She led Frappato's revival and is a leading name in natural Italian wine.
wines.concl: Very good, possibly outstanding. Intense, perfumed fruit on a light frame, fresh acidity and soft tannin in balance; long, floral finish.
wines.ready: Drink now. Can hold a few years.
exam: Cerasuolo di Vittoria is Sicily's only DOCG: a Nero d'Avola–Frappato blend. Varietal Frappato is often labelled Terre Siciliane IGT.
Light reds: pale colour, high acid, low tannin. Serve a little cool (14–16°C).
Compare across the library: Guérin Pinot, Deux Flèches Gamay and this Frappato, three light reds from three climates.
wines.say: Sicily's answer to Pinot Noir: pale, perfumed and juicy, from the winemaker who put Frappato on the map.

lineup.sub: An Alpine natural white, Lafon-family Bourgogne Blanc, California's homage to Bandol rosé and Sicily's most famous Frappato.

blocks.title: Tasting order for a flight
items: Avant la Tempête → Ode to Lulu → Lafon → Frappato.
The light Jacquère first; the rosé before the barrel-aged Chardonnay.
Serve the Frappato slightly cool and finish on it.

blocks.title: Across the library
items: Ode to Lulu vs Gros 'Noré Bandol (Nov 9): the homage vs the original. Both Mourvèdre-led and savoury.
Lafon vs Pernot Rue de Bois (Nov 3): both 2024 Bourgogne from Meursault and Puligny parcels, both in used barrels.
Jacquère vs Erbaluce (Nov 3): two Alpine-foothill whites on glacial soils.
Frappato, Gamay and Pinot Noir: the light-red trio.
